P1.evidence: The application was read and genuinely used, not just referenced - 'I did see in your form as you filled out what you would like to do. Some body fat is not your biggest priority.' The frame ran to two or three parts of four: 'Where you're at, where you want to go. See if we fit in there perfectly.' Frame agreement and open question both clean. Worth flagging as a positive: this is the only call in the batch where recording consent was explicitly requested and granted - 'Are you okay with that?' 'Yeah, yeah.'

P2.evidence: Split sharply between excellent and absent. Nutrition was the best in the batch - full macro breakdown, whole-food ratio, cheat frequency, and then a genuinely diagnostic follow-up chain about whether intake was raised at the plateau and whether fats had been tried. Injuries and mobility asked properly and specifically. Results from current training explored in depth. But age, height and weight were never asked - age only surfaced because the prospect mentioned it twice - health conditions were never raised, sleep and energy were never raised, and occupation was never established at any point on a fifty-seven-minute call that ended in a four-figure commitment.

P3.evidence: The surface work was thorough - 'What's that ten looking like for you?' produced an unusually detailed answer covering shoulders, chest, hamstrings and body fat, and the reflect-back was strong and correctly reordered: 'you want to make sure your longevity is on point, your mobility is on point... And as a byproduct of that, get in better shape.' The deep end was never asked for. The bridge question - what is actually driving this right now - was never put, and the prospect volunteered the real material himself in response to something else: 'I started to feel attractive for the first time and so much more confident... now I'm 42 and I see my youth slipping away.' Nobody else was ever asked about; after fifty-seven minutes we do not know whether he has a partner, children or anyone in his life at all, so the who-else-does-this-impact question could not be and was not run.

P4.evidence: The strongest Phase 4 in the batch and correctly adapted. Past attempts were asked for directly - 'You've gotten these programs before... you've done other 12-week programs, you've seen results with it, but of course not to the extent where you exactly want to see it yet. What do you personally feel like was missing?' - and the prospect named the gap himself twice, as tailoring and education plus a suspicion that isolation work and zero cardio caused the plateau. The rep then did real diagnostic work on the heart-rate question and the fat-intake question, which is what earned him credibility for the rest of the call. P4f does not apply: this prospect trained four to five times a week for twelve unbroken months, so stickiness is demonstrably not his problem and running 'why can't you stick to it on your own' would have been wrong.

P5.evidence: The two-year projection ran, framed forward to 52 - 'those small things do creep up on you and you start to get worse and worse and worse' - and the settle question was asked, misunderstood, and correctly re-asked until it landed: 'Well, no, absolutely not.' Neither the 'why not' follow-up nor the line-in-the-sand ask was made, and the consequence was never made concrete enough to carry weight against the price twelve minutes later.

P6.evidence: The all-in question ran properly: 'do you feel like when we get that in place, does anything that would stop you from getting to the point where you have the longevity... but also the knowledge to keep doing this yourself?' The answer contained the entire rest of the call: 'Yeah, yeah, yeah. I mean, you know, I would need to experience the program.' That is hesitation, the script says hesitation sends you back to Phase 5, and the rep instead said 'Love that. That's the right energy' and went to price. Twelve minutes later the same sentence came back as the objection that forced a trial period to be invented on the spot.

P11.evidence: The verbal yes was obtained and the link was sent, and then the phase collapsed. No payment was collected - asked 'Can I get you started now?' the prospect said 'Let me look at my numbers... I just like to think about it', and the rep accepted a promise for the next day without a further attempt. No onboarding call with Trevor was booked despite the rep saying 'we get you on board with Trevor, we'll get a meeting with him there' - both meetings actually booked are with the rep himself. No agreement email and no signature. Only the questionnaire step partly ran: 'I will send you a document over on WhatsApp... Trevor would need that for the whole onboarding as well.'

objection_plays.detail: This was the real objection and the play fits it almost exactly. The prospect had paid a year up front for a programme that underdelivered and said so: 'I don't want to, you know, do that again, especially with this one, which is more expensive' and 'I think I require some proof points in experience, to then commit the full, not only the money, but also my effort.' The script has a move written for precisely this - BURNED BEFORE, if you got hurt in a relationship once, do you never trust again - along with the certainty question, the bridge and the plane. None ran. The rep solved a trust problem with a commercial concession instead, which is why a trial period had to be invented.

Handled better than the money objections elsewhere in this batch. The isolate ran - 'Do you feel like, yes, I want to do this, we just have to look at the payment options?' - and the rep then correctly diagnosed that this was not an affordability problem: 'Is it more of a, I want to make sure I'm investing the right thing so I'm not blowing my money, or what is it sort of for you?' Having established it was not capacity, skipping the financial picture was the right call. What is missing is the HOW-not-SHOULD-I reframe, and the payment structure he settled on was invented rather than drawn from anything Primal offers.

'I just like to think about it' arrived at 00:54:33 in response to paying that day. The rep put one probe - 'where's that coming from for you? Is it just making sure or what is it for you?' - which is the right opening move. The prospect shut it down with 'I don't need to elaborate on that. I think it's a choice that I have', and the rep dropped the play entirely, said 'I'm not pressuring you to do it' and settled for a date. Respectful, and defensible given the prospect had already agreed, but none of the remaining moves ran and the money is still uncollected at the end of the recording.

notes: Excellent diagnostic selling - the plateau analysis in Phase 4 is the best work by this rep in the batch and it is what earned the yes. Two failures cost him the collection. He heard 'I would need to experience the program' at the commitment check and pressed on to price instead of going back to Phase 5, and when that same doubt returned as the objection he reached for a commercial fix rather than the fear-and-doubt play that was written for it. Then P11 was left half-run: no money, no Trevor booking, no agreement.
